picks.title: Five Controversies Sparking Endless Debate In Bhakti Culture
picks.summary: “Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. O beloved child of the Kurus, the intelligence of those who are irresolute is many-branched.” (Lord Krishna, Bhagavad-gita, 2.41)
picks.reason: Explores controversies in Bhakti culture with references to Bhagavad-gita.

picks.title: 1823: Life Is Sacred and Life Is Everywhere | The Earth Personified in Krishna's Pastimes
picks.summary: In the form of a beautiful teenager God enters a new city, meets a hunchback girl in the street, transforms her body and enters a romance with her. On the surface it sounds bizarre. But read with the right eyes, it is rich in ecological and theological depth. The girl is an expansion of Mother Earth herself, bent low under the burden of wicked rulers. Krishna straightens her out, indicates the value in loving nature personified, and demonstrates how God can reciprocate with all varieties of love. Srimad Bhagavatam 10.42. 1-18  *******************************************************************
picks.reason: Examines Krishna's pastimes with ecological and theological depth.

picks.title: Never Do An Enemy A Small Injury
picks.summary: “The thoughts of My pure devotees dwell in Me, their lives are surrendered to Me, and they derive great satisfaction and bliss enlightening one another and conversing about Me.” (Lord Krishna, Bhagavad-gita, 10.9)
picks.reason: Focuses on surrender and bliss in relation to Krishna's devotees.

Drawing on Swami Sarvapriyananda, they explore how worship, meditation, and the experience of oneness can all be part of the same spiritual journey.https://youtu.be/5Dk4EIe-qyk?is=5TBdCXYqMpaMQyNh

picks.showTitle: Chinmaya Mission - Gita, Upanishads and Ancient Knowledge
picks.title: What Lies Beyond Worldly Pleasure?| Essence of the Geeta | Episode 86
picks.summary: Swami Swaroopananda, Global Head of Chinmaya Mission, is a revered spiritual leader known for his clear, profound Vedanta teachings. His wisdom guides many towards self-discovery and inner peace, making complex concepts accessible and inspiring globally. In this series, Swamiji distills the learnings from the Bhagavad Geeta and explains it in a way that allows everyone to enjoy the essence of the Geeta.

picks.title: James D. Ryan, "The Upanisads as They Are: Brhadaranyaka, Chandogya, Aitareya, Taittiriya, Kausitaki" (Bloomsbury, 2026)
picks.summary: These Upanisads (c. 800-300 BCE) are almost always read from the point of view of the later Vedantins, but they do not share in the neatly tailored characteristics of the mature Vedantic philosophies, representing, instead, divergent, variegated and even conflicting narratives. In ﻿The Upanisads as They Are ﻿(Bloomsbury, 2026) ﻿the author focuses on the earliest of these Upanisads: Brhadaranyaka, Chandogya, Aitareya, Taittiriya, Kausitaki. picks.reason: Scholarly discussion on early Upanishads emphasizing their original, diverse meanings.
